emb:L2026478313.exclusion_reason: exploratory fMRI connectivity biomarker study derived from adult data, not a diagnostic radiology imaging application

emb:L2024393349.exclusion_reason: optical coherence tomography of ex vivo fetal membrane tissue; not a radiologic diagnostic imaging modality

emb:L2024393293.exclusion_reason: exploratory fMRI biomarker classification study for self-harm/suicide risk, not a diagnostic radiology imaging application

emb:L2023737241.clinical_problem: bone age assessment, including in patients with skeletal dysplasia
emb:L2023737241.patient_population: public RSNA bone age dataset (12,611 train / 1,425 validation / 200 test hand radiographs) plus a retrospectively collected cohort of 189 patients (568 x-rays) with molecularly confirmed genetic skeletal dysplasias
emb:L2023737241.model_description: Deeplasia is an open-source ensemble of convolutional neural networks that takes a hand radiograph as input and outputs an estimated bone age. It was trained on the public RSNA bone age dataset and additionally validated on hand x-rays from children with skeletal dysplasias, a population usually excluded from prior bone-age models, including a longitudinal subset for test-retest precision.
emb:L2023737241.release_evidence: We design and present Deeplasia, an open-source prior-free deep-learning approach for pediatric bone age assessment specifically validated on patients with skeletal dysplasias.
emb:L2023737241.dataset_size: 12,611/1,425/200 RSNA hand radiographs (train/val/test); 568 x-rays from 189 patients with skeletal dysplasias
emb:L2023737241.headline_result: mean absolute difference 3.87 months on the RSNA test set; 5.84 months on dysplastic hands; longitudinal test-retest precision 2.74 months, at least at human expert level
emb:L2023737241.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

emb:L2024392566.model_family: deep learning models (including recurrent neural networks) for tractometry-based brain-age prediction, compared to a linear baseline
emb:L2024392566.clinical_problem: predicting brain maturation (brain age) from diffusion MRI white matter measurements in children and adolescents
emb:L2024392566.patient_population: large sample of children and adolescents (exact number not stated)
emb:L2024392566.model_description: Diffusion MRI-derived white matter tract properties (tractometry) from children and adolescents were used as input to several deep learning architectures, including recurrent neural networks, to predict chronological brain age, compared against a linear regression baseline. Deep learning models, especially recurrent architectures, gave a modest accuracy improvement over the linear baseline. Open-source software implementing the models was released.
emb:L2024392566.release_evidence: We provide open-source software that fits DL models to dMRI data (https://yeatmanlab.github.io/AFQ-Insight).
emb:L2024392566.dataset_size: large sample of children and adolescents (exact N not stated)
emb:L2024392566.headline_result: recurrent neural network architectures gave up to ~6% improvement in accuracy over the linear baseline

emb:L2024392459.model_family: hierarchical Bayesian regression normative model with transfer learning
emb:L2024392459.clinical_problem: charting individual cortical thickness development, including detecting abnormal development in children born preterm, across scanners
emb:L2024392459.patient_population: reference model from N=40,435 individuals across the lifespan and dozens of sites; transferred to a longitudinal developmental cohort of children aged 6-17 years (N=5,985) with three measurement waves on two scanners
emb:L2024392459.model_description: A large reference normative model of cortical thickness was estimated with hierarchical Bayesian regression from over 40,000 individuals across the lifespan, then transferred to a longitudinal cohort of children aged 6-17 scanned on two scanners not seen during model estimation. The model produces an individual deviation score for cortical thickness that is independent of scanner effects, and was shown to detect morphological heterogeneity in individuals born preterm.
emb:L2024392459.dataset_size: reference model N=40,435 (all ages); transfer cohort N=5,985 children aged 6-17, three waves, two scanners
emb:L2024392459.headline_result: a transfer set of as few as 25 samples per site gave good performance; deviation scores detected morphological heterogeneity in individuals born pre-term
emb:L2024392459.study_design: retrospective multi-site longitudinal normative modeling study

emb:L2021801016.model_family: Generative Adversarial Network (autoencoder generator with residual/SE blocks, CNN discriminator)
emb:L2021801016.clinical_problem: correcting motion artifacts in fetal MRI to avoid repeat scanning
emb:L2021801016.patient_population: fetal MRI; trained on a synthetically created motion-artifact dataset and validated on real motion-degraded fetal MRI scans (exact number not stated)
emb:L2021801016.model_description: A GAN-based deep learning network, trained on a synthetically generated motion-artifact fetal MRI dataset created by modifying k-space data, reduces and removes motion artifacts. It takes a motion-degraded fetal MR image as input and outputs a corrected image, and was also evaluated on real motion-affected scans.
emb:L2021801016.dataset_size: synthetic motion-artifact training set (N not stated); validated on real motion-degraded fetal MRI scans
emb:L2021801016.headline_result: average SSIM 93.7% and PSNR 33.5 dB on the synthetic dataset; average BRISQUE score 21.1 on real motion-affected images; outperformed BM3D, RED-Net, NLM filtering, and WGAN-VGG

emb:L2021883301.exclusion_reason: EEG-based classification study; EEG is not a diagnostic radiology imaging modality

emb:L2026970737.clinical_problem: bone age assessment from hand radiographs
emb:L2026970737.patient_population: children undergoing hand radiography (RSNA public bone age dataset)
emb:L2026970737.model_description: Hand radiographs from the RSNA bone age dataset were preprocessed and used to fine-tune a pre-trained DenseNet-121 convolutional neural network via transfer learning. The model outputs an estimated bone age from a hand radiograph, intended to assist radiologists with faster, less observer-dependent skeletal maturity assessment.
emb:L2026970737.dataset_size: RSNA public hand radiograph bone age dataset (exact split not stated)
emb:L2026970737.headline_result: mean absolute error of 9.8 months, the best of five pre-trained models evaluated
emb:L2026970737.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

emb:L2023326618.model_family: support vector machine classification on HARDI diffusion MRI features, with TBSS and canonical correlation analysis
emb:L2023326618.clinical_problem: identifying white matter alterations associated with preterm birth
emb:L2023326618.patient_population: 46 preterm infants imaged at term-equivalent age and 23 control neonates born at term
emb:L2023326618.model_description: Advanced diffusion MRI (HARDI) measures from preterm and term-born neonates were analyzed with a traditional voxel-wise statistical method (TBSS) and a support vector machine classifier to identify white matter regions that discriminate preterm from term birth, with canonical correlation analysis relating findings across imaging measures.
emb:L2023326618.headline_result: SVM classification on skeletonized HARDI measures produced satisfactory accuracy, especially for fiber-directionality parameters (no single summary number reported)

emb:L2019064810.model_family: unrolled neural network (modified DL-ESPIRiT) with Complex Difference estimation
emb:L2019064810.clinical_problem: accelerating cardiac MRI flow quantification (peak velocity, total flow) to reduce scan time in children
emb:L2019064810.patient_population: 155 fully sampled pediatric clinical 2D phase-contrast MRI datasets for training; prospective pediatric clinical patients for feasibility testing
emb:L2019064810.model_description: A deep learning reconstruction framework (CD-DL) was trained on 155 fully sampled pediatric 2D phase-contrast cardiac MRI datasets to reconstruct highly undersampled (6-11x accelerated) flow images. It takes undersampled k-space data as input and outputs reconstructed images with quantitative peak velocity and total flow measurements, evaluated against a parallel imaging/compressed sensing method and tested prospectively in pediatric patients.
emb:L2019064810.dataset_size: 155 fully sampled pediatric 2D phase-contrast MRI datasets (training); prospective pediatric cohort for feasibility testing (N not stated)
emb:L2019064810.headline_result: 9x accelerated CD-DL reconstruction was accurate and precise for peak velocity (bias 2.8 vs 3.9 for PICS) and total flow (1.8 vs 2.9 for PICS)
emb:L2019064810.study_design: retrospective and prospective technical validation study

emb:L2021723553.clinical_problem: automated segmentation of standard fetal ultrasound scanning planes to measure biometric parameters
emb:L2021723553.model_description: This survey reviews 2D and 3D fetal ultrasound image segmentation methods for measuring standard biometric parameters, grouped into deep learning-based, other machine learning-based, active contour-based, and thresholding-based approaches, discussing advantages, limitations, and future potential for remote obstetric monitoring.

emb:L2021967048.clinical_problem: real-time detection of fetal cardiac substructures on ultrasound for prenatal cardiac assessment
emb:L2021967048.model_description: A YOLOv7-based end-to-end neural network was trained on 40 fetal echocardiography videos to simultaneously detect nine fetal cardiac substructures (e.g. atria, ventricles, valves, aorta) as bounding boxes in real time from 2D ultrasound video, aiming to support real-time interpretation of fetal cardiac anatomy.
emb:L2021967048.headline_result: highest mean average precision 82.10% at 17 frames per second (0.3 ms per frame) across nine cardiac substructures

emb:L2022786744.model_family: vendor deep learning reconstruction (DLR) compared with ASIR-V iterative reconstruction
emb:L2022786744.clinical_problem: improving image quality / reducing radiation dose for pediatric brain CT
emb:L2022786744.model_description: Brain CT data from 61 children were reconstructed with six levels of adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V) and three levels of deep learning reconstruction (DLR: low, middle, high). Signal-to-noise ratio, contrast-to-noise ratio, noise, and subjective 5-point image quality scores were compared to determine which reconstruction level best preserves diagnostic image quality.
emb:L2022786744.headline_result: DLR-high noise reduction rate exceeded ASIR-V100% (supratentorial 0.62 vs 0.59, infratentorial 0.61 vs 0.59, both P<0.001); DLR-middle and DLR-high had higher subjective scores than all ASIR-V levels

emb:L2023824656.clinical_problem: reducing radiation dose while maintaining image quality in pediatric CT
emb:L2023824656.model_description: This review summarizes progress in deep learning-based iterative CT image reconstruction techniques and their application to pediatric CT, framed around maintaining diagnostic image quality while minimizing radiation dose in children.

emb:L2023971360.model_family: deep learning (DL) PET image reconstruction platform
emb:L2023971360.clinical_problem: reducing scan time/radiotracer dose for pediatric 18F-FDG PET/CT while preserving image quality
emb:L2023971360.model_description: In 93 children, standard full-dose (120 s/bed) and fast (20 s/bed) whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT scans were acquired, and 20 s/bed images were also extracted in list mode from the full-dose acquisition. All short-duration images were processed through a deep learning reconstruction platform to produce full-dose-equivalent images, and image-quality metrics and standardized uptake values were compared across the resulting image sets.
emb:L2023971360.headline_result: no significant differences in subjective quality score, TBR, CNR, CV, SUVmax, or SUVmean between standard 120s and DL-reconstructed 20s images (all P>0.05)
emb:L2023971360.study_design: retrospective single-center diagnostic performance comparison study

emb:L2024754376.exclusion_reason: general review of pediatric lung MRI techniques; AI mentioned only briefly as a future direction, not the subject of the review

emb:L2025133072.exclusion_reason: general review of hip ultrasound DDH screening programs; AI imaging technology mentioned only in passing, not the focus

emb:L2025579294.model_family: AI-assisted TW3 (Tanner-Whitehouse 3) bone age assessment system
emb:L2025579294.clinical_problem: bone age assessment using TW3-Carpal vs TW3-RUS scoring criteria
emb:L2025579294.patient_population: 262 children who underwent left wrist radiography, stratified into six 3-year age groups spanning 1-18 years
emb:L2025579294.model_description: Left wrist radiographs from 262 children were assessed for bone age with an AI-assisted system using two different scoring criteria, TW3-Carpal and TW3-RUS, and compared against the averaged assessment of two senior pediatric radiologists as reference, across six age strata.
emb:L2025579294.headline_result: ICC 0.983 (TW3-RUS) and 0.976 (TW3-Carpal) vs reference; TW3-RUS criteria performed better for ages 10-15, TW3-Carpal better for ages 4-9

emb:L2025579295.model_family: deep learning bone age prediction software
emb:L2025579295.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in children with abnormal growth and development
emb:L2025579295.patient_population: 717 children with abnormal growth and development (266 male, 451 female), aged 2-18 years
emb:L2025579295.model_description: Left wrist radiographs from 717 children with abnormal growth and development were evaluated for bone age using the Dr. Wise AI bone age prediction software (TW3-RUS and TW3-Carpal methods), compared against a reference standard (mean of three senior radiologists) and against two junior radiologists.
emb:L2025579295.release_evidence: the AI system (Dr. Wise bone age prediction software)
emb:L2025579295.headline_result: AI accuracy within 0.5 year: 75.3% (TW3-RUS) and 80.9% (TW3-Carpal); lower mean absolute error than junior radiologists (e.g. 0.360 vs 0.565/0.496 years, P<0.001), comparable agreement with senior radiologists (ICC>0.95)

emb:L2025579305.clinical_problem: bone age assessment using artificial intelligence
emb:L2025579305.model_description: This review (no abstract provided) covers the application and development of artificial intelligence methods for bone age imaging assessment in children, based on the title alone.

emb:L2027015291.model_family: radiomics-based nomogram (mRMR/LASSO feature selection, multivariate logistic regression) combining clinical and MRI radiomics features
emb:L2027015291.clinical_problem: differentiating idiopathic central precocious puberty from premature thelarche
emb:L2027015291.patient_population: 118 children (67 with idiopathic central precocious puberty, 51 with premature thelarche), split into training (n=83) and validation (n=35) sets
emb:L2027015291.model_description: Clinical variables (age, bone age, body mass, hormone levels) and radiomics features from sagittal pituitary T1-weighted MRI were combined into a nomogram to distinguish idiopathic central precocious puberty from premature thelarche in girls, using feature selection (mRMR, LASSO) and logistic regression, compared against clinical-only and radiomics-only models.
emb:L2027015291.headline_result: combined nomogram AUC 0.981 (training) and 0.977 (validation), better than the clinical-only model (P<0.05), similar to the radiomics-only model
emb:L2027015291.study_design: retrospective single-center diagnostic model development study

emb:L2027015310.model_family: deep learning image classification/landmark model for standard-plane recognition and measurement
emb:L2027015310.clinical_problem: automated identification of the standard hip ultrasound plane and measurement of alpha angle, beta angle, and femoral head coverage for DDH screening
emb:L2027015310.patient_population: 2,164 infants (4,328 hips) undergoing bilateral hip ultrasound
emb:L2027015310.model_description: An AI model was trained on 8,100 annotated hip ultrasound images from 2,164 infants to automatically recognize the standard coronal plane of the hip joint and measure alpha angle, beta angle, and femoral head coverage, parameters used in developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) screening. Its standard-plane recognition and measurements were compared with manual selection and measurement by ultrasound physicians.
emb:L2027015310.dataset_size: 11,100 images from 2,164 infants (4,328 hips): 8,100 training / 3,000 validation, plus 220 images from 110 additional infants for measurement comparison
emb:L2027015310.headline_result: AI standard-plane recognition agreement with chief physicians Kappa=0.925; measurement ICC 0.814 (alpha angle), 0.730 (beta angle), 0.953 (femoral head coverage) vs manual measurement

emb:L2028211224.clinical_problem: AI-assisted prenatal ultrasound examination of the fetal central nervous system and cardiac anatomy
emb:L2028211224.model_description: This review discusses how automated segmentation techniques for 2D and 3D ultrasound images are applied throughout the prenatal ultrasound workflow, with AI shown to assist targeted examination of the fetal central nervous system, fetal cardiac anatomy, and quantification of cardiac functional parameters, and notes that clinical implementation requires validated tools and adequately trained staff.

emb:L2028492478.clinical_problem: automated quality control of the standard mid-sagittal fetal face view for first-trimester nuchal translucency screening
emb:L2028492478.patient_population: 1,063 fetal nuchal translucency ultrasound image sections at 11-13+6 weeks of gestation
emb:L2028492478.model_description: An online AI quality-control system evaluated whether fetal nuchal translucency ultrasound mid-sagittal face images at 11-13+6 weeks gestation met standard imaging criteria. Its assessments were compared against manual quality control by two experts, with a senior expert panel as the gold standard, and time efficiency was also compared.
emb:L2028492478.headline_result: overall accuracy 96.6%; agreement with two experts Kappa 0.835 and 0.845; AI quality control took 208 s vs 6,696/6,602 s for manual review (P<0.001)

emb:L2028492502.model_family: deep learning model (transfer learning) for automated tomographic plane extraction
emb:L2028492502.clinical_problem: automated extraction of the standard retronasal triangle plane for fetal palate screening at 11-13+6 weeks
emb:L2028492502.patient_population: 235 normal fetuses at 11-13+6 weeks of gestation
emb:L2028492502.model_description: 3D ultrasound volumes from 235 normal fetuses at 11-13+6 weeks were used to train a deep learning model, via transfer learning, to automatically extract the retronasal triangle plane for fetal palate assessment. Model output was compared with manual tomographic imaging performed by sonographers, evaluating plane quality score, acquisition rate, and time required.
emb:L2028492502.headline_result: no significant difference in retronasal triangle plane quality score between sonographer and AI groups (both median 5, P=0.722); AI required 1.50s vs 26.94s for sonographers (P<0.001)

emb:L2028492524.model_family: radiomics-based logistic regression model (LASSO/stepwise feature selection)
emb:L2028492524.clinical_problem: diagnosing white matter injury in premature infants from cranial ultrasound
emb:L2028492524.model_description: Radiomics features were extracted from standardized craniocerebral ultrasound images of 256 premature infants, and a logistic regression model was built after feature selection to diagnose white matter injury, using MRI as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance of the radiomics model was compared with, and used to assist, junior and senior sonographers.
emb:L2028492524.headline_result: validation set AUC 0.876, comparable to senior sonographer (0.910, P=0.284) and better than junior sonographer (0.729, P=0.001); radiomics assistance raised junior sonographer AUC to 0.841 (P=0.003)

emb:L2029836242.clinical_problem: automated analysis of standard prenatal ultrasound scanning planes
emb:L2029836242.model_description: This review summarizes research progress applying deep learning to prenatal ultrasound section (scanning plane) analysis, focused on segmentation and recognition tasks that extract higher-level image features to address operator dependence and imaging variability in fetal ultrasound screening.

emb:L2022075794.model_family: deep learning-based automated cerebellar parcellation (segmentation) applied to structural MRI, with diffusion tensor imaging analysis
emb:L2022075794.clinical_problem: quantifying secondary cerebellar volume changes after pediatric moderate-severe traumatic brain injury and their relation to executive function
emb:L2022075794.patient_population: 598 children and adolescents with (n=314) or without (n=284) moderate-severe TBI, mean age 14.0±3.1 years, pooled from 12 datasets (ENIGMA Pediatric msTBI working group)
emb:L2022075794.model_description: A deep learning-based automated parcellation method was applied to structural MRI to measure total cerebellar volume and 17 subregion volumes in 598 children and adolescents with and without moderate-severe traumatic brain injury, pooled across 12 multi-site datasets. Cerebellar volumes were related to executive function scores and, in a longitudinal subsample, to early diffusion tensor imaging white matter measures, to characterize secondary cerebellar changes after pediatric brain injury.
emb:L2022075794.dataset_size: 598 children and adolescents (314 msTBI, 284 non-TBI) from 12 pooled datasets; longitudinal subsample n=80
emb:L2022075794.headline_result: smaller total cerebellar volume in msTBI (Cohen's d=-0.37), most pronounced in posterior lobe/vermis regions (d=-0.22 to -0.43); smaller cerebellar volume associated with more parent-reported executive function problems
emb:L2022075794.study_design: retrospective multi-site cross-sectional and longitudinal imaging study

emb:L2022245969.model_family: 3D convolutional neural network ensemble (Bayesian-optimized, K-fold cross-validated)
emb:L2022245969.clinical_problem: measuring fetal intracranial volume to study prenatal brain growth and sex differences
emb:L2022245969.patient_population: 168 annotated 3D ultrasound scans for model development; applied to N=9,795 ultrasounds from 1,763 participants at 20- and 30-week gestational age
emb:L2022245969.model_description: A 3D convolutional neural network ensemble was trained on 168 annotated 3D fetal ultrasound scans, using data augmentation, K-fold cross-validation, and Bayesian optimization, to automatically segment fetal intracranial volume (ICV). The trained model was applied to a large independent longitudinal cohort (9,795 ultrasounds, 1,763 participants at 20 and 30 weeks gestation) to measure ICV and study sex differences in fetal brain growth.
emb:L2022245969.dataset_size: 168 annotated 3D ultrasound scans for training; 9,795 ultrasounds from 1,763 participants for the applied study
emb:L2022245969.headline_result: boys had significantly larger ICV at 20 weeks (B=2.83, p=1.4e-13) and 30 weeks (B=12.01, p=2.0e-28), with more pronounced ICV growth than girls (t=-4.395, p=1.3e-5)

emb:L2022075312.exclusion_reason: landscape/bibliometric analysis of FDA-approved AI/ML devices; does not develop or evaluate a specific imaging AI model

emb:L2018891055.clinical_problem: measuring fetal head circumference and biparietal diameter for gestational age estimation and CNS assessment
emb:L2018891055.patient_population: 102 labeled training images and 70 test ultrasound images
emb:L2018891055.model_description: A multi-task deep convolutional neural network was trained to simultaneously segment the fetal head and fit an ellipse for head circumference and biparietal diameter estimation from ultrasound images, jointly optimizing a segmentation dice score and an ellipse-parameter error term. The model takes a 2D fetal head ultrasound image as input and outputs the head boundary and biometric measurements.
emb:L2018891055.headline_result: success rate 92.31% for HC/BPD estimation; 87.14% accuracy for standard-plane acceptance check

emb:L2020057769.clinical_problem: fetal brain segmentation, classifying pathological vs neurotypical brain, and estimating gestational age from fetal brain MRI
emb:L2020057769.model_description: MTSE U-Net is a multi-tasking single-encoder U-Net that, from an already-extracted fetal brain MRI, simultaneously segments the brain into seven structures (intracranial/extra-axial CSF spaces, gray matter, white matter, ventricles, cerebellum, deep gray matter, brainstem and spinal cord), classifies the brain as pathological or neurotypical, and predicts gestational age, all with a single shared model.
emb:L2020057769.headline_result: Jaccard similarity 77% and Dice score 82% for segmentation; 89% accuracy for pathological/neurotypical classification; mean absolute error 0.83 weeks for gestational age prediction

emb:L2020057910.clinical_problem: AI-assisted detection of fetal brain and cardiovascular abnormalities on fetal MRI
emb:L2020057910.model_description: This review summarizes advances in applying artificial intelligence to fetal brain and cardiac MRI, an area with far fewer published studies than AI applied to fetal ultrasound, and discusses how AI tools may assist clinicians and parents in decision-making around central nervous system and cardiovascular abnormalities.

emb:L2021629380.model_family: machine learning classifier on diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) white matter features
emb:L2021629380.body_region: brain (auditory and cognitive white matter pathways)
emb:L2021629380.clinical_problem: predicting speech perception improvement after cochlear implantation in children
emb:L2021629380.patient_population: young cochlear implant candidates compared with matched normal-hearing children (exact N not stated)
emb:L2021629380.model_description: Pre-surgical diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) was compared between pediatric cochlear implant (CI) candidates and normal-hearing children to identify affected cortical regions. A machine learning model then used non-imaging and DTI-derived white matter features (whole-brain, affected, and unaffected regions) to predict whether a child would have high or low improvement in speech perception 6 months after implantation.
emb:L2021629380.headline_result: prediction using unaffected white matter regions: accuracy 0.86, sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.80; whole-brain white matter similar (0.85/0.91/0.80), both better than affected regions (0.72/0.74/0.70) and non-imaging features alone (0.67/0.55/0.78)

emb:L2021629543.exclusion_reason: community depression sample; pediatric/adolescent age range not stated in the abstract

emb:L2022233933.model_family: vendor deep learning reconstruction (DLR) compared with ASIR-V iterative reconstruction
emb:L2022233933.clinical_problem: reducing radiation dose in pediatric craniocerebral trauma CT while maintaining diagnostic image quality
emb:L2022233933.patient_population: 51 children with craniocerebral trauma and intracerebral hemorrhage undergoing low-dose brain CT
emb:L2022233933.model_description: Low-dose brain CT data from 51 children with traumatic intracerebral hemorrhage were reconstructed at two slice thicknesses with three levels of adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V) and three levels of deep learning reconstruction (DLR: low, middle, high). Objective image-quality metrics and subjective 5-point scores were compared across reconstruction methods to identify the best approach for low-dose pediatric head CT.
emb:L2022233933.headline_result: 1.25 mm DLR-high images had higher SNR/CNR than 100% ASIR-V (P<0.05); DLR-middle and DLR-high subjective scores exceeded all ASIR-V levels, meeting diagnostic quality thresholds that thin-slice ASIR-V did not

emb:L2021043977.model_family: linear mixed-effect models for regional brain-size analysis; support vector machine for outcome prediction
emb:L2021043977.clinical_problem: characterizing early brain structural alterations in autism and predicting later language outcome
emb:L2021043977.patient_population: 166 autistic and 109 typically developing toddlers (intake mean age 2.5 years); replicated in 38 autistic and 37 typically developing toddlers
emb:L2021043977.model_description: Structural MRI from toddlers with and without autism (discovery cohort plus an independent replication cohort) was used to measure regional gray matter volume, cortical surface area, and thickness with linear mixed-effect models, identifying replicable regional alterations related to symptom severity and cognitive scores. A support vector machine model then tested whether adding these early brain-size measures to intake clinical and behavioral data improved prediction of language outcome at ages 3-4.
emb:L2021043977.dataset_size: 166 autistic and 109 typically developing toddlers (discovery); 38 autistic and 37 typically developing toddlers (replication)
emb:L2021043977.headline_result: adding early regional brain-size measures to the SVM model improved accuracy for predicting later language outcome beyond intake clinical and demographic variables (no single accuracy figure given)

emb:L2021262181.exclusion_reason: computational language model study benchmarked against adult fMRI data; 'developmental' refers to training-data size analogy, not pediatric imaging subjects

emb:L2019443913.clinical_problem: use of AI and simulation to improve prenatal ultrasound education and training
emb:L2019443913.model_description: This review presents an overview of current applications of artificial intelligence and simulation techniques in prenatal ultrasound medicine, with a focus on their potential to improve education and training, and advocates integrating structured simulation-based ultrasound training into training curricula.

emb:L2019443927.model_description: This review provides an overview of the current state of development of artificial intelligence, particularly neural networks, for automated analysis of prenatal diagnostic ultrasound images, and summarizes which AI technologies are already used in prenatal diagnosis.

emb:L2020587349.exclusion_reason: MR fingerprinting technical development study; pediatric relevance mentioned only as motivation, study population not stated as pediatric

emb:L2020674154.model_family: 3D convolutional neural network (U-Net) within a BIDS-App Snakemake workflow
emb:L2020674154.clinical_problem: automated brain masking/segmentation for fetal functional MRI analysis
emb:L2020674154.patient_population: 159 fetuses (1,103 volumes) from open-access data for training/testing; 19 fetuses (82 scans, over 2,300 volumes) from a local cohort for generalizability testing
emb:L2020674154.model_description: Funcmasker-flex is an open-source BIDS App that uses a 3D U-Net convolutional neural network to automatically segment (mask) the fetal brain from functional MRI volumes, removing the need for manual segmentation. It was trained and tested on open-access fetal fMRI data from 159 fetuses and further validated for generalizability on a separate local cohort of 19 fetuses.
emb:L2020674154.release_evidence: The tool is freely available and can be applied to any BIDS dataset containing fetal bold sequences.
emb:L2020674154.dataset_size: 159 fetuses / 1,103 volumes (training/testing); 19 fetuses / 82 scans / >2,300 volumes (generalizability testing)
emb:L2020674154.headline_result: Dice metrics consistently ≥0.74 across both datasets compared to manual segmentation
emb:L2020674154.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

emb:L2018658371.model_family: deep learning object detection for vertebral landmark localization
emb:L2018658371.clinical_problem: monitoring spinal curvature (Cobb angle) in scoliosis without radiation exposure
emb:L2018658371.patient_population: adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients (phantom and in vivo validation; exact N not stated)
emb:L2018658371.model_description: A deep learning object-detection method locates vertebral landmarks from freehand tracked ultrasound B-scan sequences of the spine; the landmarks are clustered to estimate the size, location, and posture of each vertebra, with missing vertebrae interpolated using anatomical priors, reconstructing a 3D model of the whole spine and measuring the Cobb angle without radiographs. The method was tested with phantom and in vivo experiments in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients.
emb:L2018658371.headline_result: Cobb angle measurement correlation R2=0.978 (P<0.001) against reference
emb:L2018658371.study_design: technical development and phantom/in vivo validation study

emb:L2019968141.exclusion_reason: narrative review of AI/ML in pediatric epilepsy focused on EEG seizure detection, not diagnostic imaging

emb:L2019770662.exclusion_reason: animal (rhesus monkey) study, not a human pediatric population

emb:L2018333015.exclusion_reason: conceptual review of music, prenatal sound perception, and AI; not a diagnostic radiology imaging application

emb:L2019914327.model_family: convolutional neural network with dropout in the convolutional layers (custom architecture)
emb:L2019914327.patient_population: pediatric patients aged 1-5 years from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center (public dataset)
emb:L2019914327.model_description: A convolutional neural network using dropout within its convolutional layers was trained and tested on 5,856 labeled pediatric anterior-posterior chest radiographs (a public dataset originally from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center, ages 1-5) to automatically detect pneumonia.
emb:L2019914327.headline_result: 97.2% accuracy, 97.3% recall, 97.4% precision, AUC 0.982, competitive with current state-of-the-art solutions
emb:L2019914327.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

emb:L2019455782.clinical_problem: improving MRI spatial resolution without longer scan times, tested for generalizability across populations including newborns
emb:L2019455782.patient_population: three cohorts: older subjects, newborns, and patients with brain tumor- or treatment-induced tissue changes
emb:L2019455782.model_description: Super Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks (SRGANs) were trained on T1-weighted MRI from three cohorts (older adults, newborns, and brain tumor patients) to upsample image resolution, and tested for generalizability when applied across cohorts and when trained on a combined multi-cohort dataset, using synthetic and anatomical quality metrics.
emb:L2019455782.headline_result: no artifacts were introduced when SRGANs were applied across cohorts or trained on a combined dataset; high image quality and anatomical fidelity were maintained

emb:L2019455434.exclusion_reason: basic developmental neuroscience study of cortical activity propagation in typically developing youth; no diagnostic imaging application or disease population

emb:L2019149874.exclusion_reason: functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) study; not a standard diagnostic radiology imaging modality

emb:L2017206162.model_family: convolutional neural networks with an iterative vertebra-localization algorithm
emb:L2017206162.clinical_problem: automated measurement of Cobb angle for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
emb:L2017206162.patient_population: adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients; 110 and 272 radiographs used to train two CNNs, 100 new radiographs used for evaluation
emb:L2017206162.model_description: Two convolutional neural networks, trained on 110 and 272 posteroanterior spine radiographs, segment the spinal column and individual vertebrae; combined with an iterative vertebra-localization algorithm, they automatically calculate the Cobb angle for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. Automatic measurements on 100 new radiographs were compared with manual measurements.
emb:L2017206162.dataset_size: 110 and 272 training radiographs for the two CNNs; 100 additional radiographs for evaluation
emb:L2017206162.headline_result: mean absolute difference 2.8°±2.8° vs manual measurement; 88% of measurements within 5° of manual measurement; average processing time 90 seconds per image

emb:L636766776.model_family: unsupervised machine learning (k-means clustering) on chest CT radiomics features
emb:L636766776.clinical_problem: predicting and evaluating treatment response to lumacaftor-ivacaftor in cystic fibrosis using lung CT phenotypes
emb:L636766776.patient_population: 283 adolescents and adults with cystic fibrosis from a French multi-center prospective study, with baseline and 1-year follow-up chest CT
emb:L636766776.model_description: In 283 adolescents and adults with cystic fibrosis starting lumacaftor-ivacaftor therapy, chest CT before and after 1 year of treatment was visually scored with a modified Bhalla score, and 120 radiomics features from pre-treatment CT were used in unsupervised k-means clustering to identify morphological lung-disease phenotypes. The resulting clusters were tested for association with lung function (FEV1) improvement on treatment.
emb:L636766776.headline_result: Bhalla score decreased significantly after 1 year (-1.40±1.53 points, P<0.001); cluster C patients more likely to have ≥5% FEV1 improvement than other clusters (54% vs 32% and 33%, P=0.02)

emb:L2018694748.exclusion_reason: gestational age estimation from newborn screening blood metabolites; non-imaging method

emb:L2018694430.model_family: convolutional neural network (deep learning brain-age prediction)
emb:L2018694430.clinical_problem: linking pubertal development to brain maturation via brain-age prediction
emb:L2018694430.patient_population: children aged 9-12 years from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, assessed longitudinally at two timepoints
emb:L2018694430.model_description: A convolutional neural network deep learning brain-age model was trained on minimally processed T1-weighted structural MRI from the large longitudinal ABCD cohort (children aged 9-12) to predict each child's brain age at two timepoints. Predicted brain age was related to pubertal stage using linear mixed-effects models to test whether pubertal development is associated with accelerated brain maturation.
emb:L2018694430.dataset_size: ABCD cohort, children aged 9-12, two longitudinal timepoints (exact N not stated in excerpt)
emb:L2018694430.headline_result: brain-age prediction mean absolute error 0.7 and 1.4 years at the two timepoints, ICC 0.65; each pubertal-stage advance associated with 2.4 months higher brain age (β=0.10, P<.001), with steeper brain-age increases at higher pubertal development rates (P<.001)
